manifest.name: Margins by Products
manifest.description: Adds a reporting menu in products that computes sales, purchases, margins and other interesting indicators based on invoices.
manifest.author: Odoo S.A.

models.kind: TransientModel (wizard, has DB table but transient)

models._description: Product Variant (inherit; adds 17 non-stored computed margin fields)
models.note: All 17 added fields are compute='_compute_product_margin_fields_values', store=False (purely runtime/in-memory); no new column is created. The compute reads context keys date_from/date_to/invoice_state set by the product.margin wizard. The model is NOT _auto=False (it is the real product.product table) but these particular fields behave like a virtual SQL-view layered over account.move.line.

security.note: Single ir.model.access row: model_product_margin granted read/write/create (no unlink) to account.group_account_user. No record rules; the margin fields ride on product.product's own security. The reporting menu sits under account.account_reports_management_menu, so it is reachable only by Accounting users.

views.note: Two forms (the product.margin wizard form product_margin_form_view; and view_product_margin_form, a product.product Margins form with Sales/Purchases/Margins notebook page). One list view_product_margin_tree with column sums (Turnover/Sales Gap/Total Cost/Total Margin) and progressbar widgets on the two margin-rate fields. One graph view_product_margin_graph plotting total_margin as a measure grouped by product_tmpl_id. The wizard's act_window product_margin_act_window opens target=new; action_open_window then re-opens product.product in list,form,graph with the date/state context injected.

behavioral_notes.observation: The whole module's substance. For self.ids it runs ONE parametrised SQL statement TWICE (invoice_types ('out_invoice','out_refund') for sales, then ('in_invoice','in_refund') for purchases) against account_move_line l JOIN account_move i JOIN product_product JOIN product_template pt, wrapped in a MATERIALIZED currency_rate CTE from res.currency._select_companies_rates() so multi-currency invoice amounts are converted to company currency. Refund lines are netted by the CASE move_type IN ('out_invoice','in_invoice') THEN 1 ELSE -1 sign. Per product it derives: avg_unit_price = SUM(price_subtotal/rate*sign)/NULLIF(SUM(qty*sign),0) -> sale_avg_price / purchase_avg_price; num_qty -> sale_num_invoiced / purchase_num_invoiced; total (signed -balance) -> turnover (sales) and total_cost (purchases); and SUM(qty*pt.list_price*sign) -> sale_expected (catalog price x invoiced qty). The compute is gated by invoice_state -> (state, payment_state) filter sets: 'paid' = posted & {in_payment,paid,reversed}; 'open_paid' = posted & {not_paid,in_payment,paid,reversed,partial}; 'draft_open_paid' = adds draft state. Filtered by i.invoice_date BETWEEN date_from AND date_to (defaults this calendar year), i.company_id = force_company|env.company, and l.display_type='product'. None of this exists in metadata - the field list shows 14 Floats with no hint they are SQL aggregates.

behavioral_notes.element: product.product margin formulas (the metadata gap: derived KPIs)
behavioral_notes.observation: After the two SQL passes, the Python derives the headline margin KPIs from the raw aggregates: normal_cost = product.standard_price * purchase_num_invoiced (expected cost at the cost-price, NOT the actually-billed total_cost); sales_gap = sale_expected - turnover (catalog vs realised revenue); purchase_gap = normal_cost - total_cost (expected vs realised cost); total_margin = turnover - total_cost (realised margin); expected_margin = sale_expected - normal_cost (catalog/theoretical margin); total_margin_rate = total_margin*100/turnover and expected_margin_rate = expected_margin*100/sale_expected (both guarded against /0 with the and/or idiom). So 'expected' figures are theoretical (catalog list_price x cost standard_price) while 'total/turnover' figures are what invoices actually booked - the report's whole point is the gap between the two, which is pure Python arithmetic invisible to the schema.

product.margin is a TransientModel (3 fields: from_date, to_date, invoice_state default 'open_paid'). It owns no margin data itself. action_open_window (ensure_one) looks up the product search view plus the three product_margin.* product.product views by xml_id, copies the env context with create=False/edit=False, injects date_from=from_date, date_to=to_date and invoice_state=self.invoice_state, and returns an ir.actions.act_window on res_model='product.product' with view_mode 'list,form,graph'. Those context keys are exactly what _compute_product_margin_fields_values reads, so the wizard is purely a parameter form that re-launches product.product in 'margin mode' for the chosen period/state. There is no product.margin table of results.

Because the 17 margin fields are store=False, Odoo's grouping/SQL layer cannot SUM them in the database. The override declares _SPECIAL_SUM_AGGREGATES = {'<field>:sum' for the 13 numeric margin fields}; _read_group_select returns SQL('NULL') for those specs so _description_aggregator() does not fail; then _read_group/_read_grouping_sets fall back to fetching the matching records (adding 'id:recordset'), force-computing them in Python via self._fields['turnover'].compute_value(all_records) (which triggers the shared compute) to bypass PREFETCH_MAX batching, and replace each NULL aggregate with sum(records.mapped(field_name)). This is how the list view's sum='Turnover'/'Total Margin' columns and the graph measure get totals for fields that have no column - a Python-side group-by-sum shim, entirely invisible to metadata.

it_architecture.application: product_margin (Margins by Products analytical reporting component over account invoices)
logical_data_erm: product.product -> account.move.line (read via raw SQL on l.product_id)
information_flows: depends: account (account.move / account.move.line are the sole data source)

flow: user opens Product Margins wizard (product.margin) -> picks from_date/to_date/invoice_state -> action_open_window injects date_from/date_to/invoice_state into context -> product.product list/form/graph
side-effect: rendering product.product margin fields -> _compute_product_margin_fields_values fires raw SQL twice (sales + purchases) over account_move_line -> 17 computed KPIs
side-effect: list-sum / graph-measure on margin fields -> _read_group / _read_grouping_sets Python shim computes group totals for non-stored fields
no outbound integration, no routes, no stored result table

capabilities: Compute Product Sales/Purchase Margins from Invoices
Parameterise Margin Analysis by Date Range & Invoice State
Quantify Sales & Purchase Gaps per Product
Visualise Margin by Product (list sums / graph measure)
value_streams: Analyse-Margin: choose period + invoice state in the product.margin wizard -> system aggregates customer-invoice and vendor-bill lines per product -> derive turnover, costs, expected vs realised margins and rates -> present as list (with sums), form (KPI sheet) and graph for decision-making
organization: account.group_account_user (Accounting user - the only group granted access to the wizard and the report menu)
policies: invoice_state policy: 'paid' / 'open_paid' (default) / 'draft_open_paid' maps to the set of account.move state + payment_state included in the aggregation
expected vs realised policy: 'expected' KPIs use catalog list_price and cost standard_price; 'total/turnover' KPIs use actually-invoiced amounts; the report exposes the gap
company scoping: aggregation restricted to env.company (or context force_company); multi-currency normalised via currency_rate CTE
line scoping: only l.display_type='product' lines counted; refunds netted by move_type sign
stakeholders: Sales & Purchasing management (consume the margin KPIs)
Product Manager (catalog list_price / standard_price feed expected margins)
metrics: turnover (sum of invoiced sale price x qty)
total_cost (sum of vendor-bill price x qty)

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (cost/profitability analysis), secondary 2.0 Develop and Manage Products and Services
classification.rationale: product_margin is a read-only analytical/management-reporting overlay, not an operational document flow: it creates no business object (product.margin is a throwaway TransientModel parameter form) and owns no stored data - it just aggregates existing account.move.line records into per-product margin KPIs on the fly. That is a firm-infrastructure SUPPORT activity (Stabell & Fjeldstad support / Porter management-accounting support), feeding decisions in the primary chain (sale/purchase) rather than performing them. APQC: the work is product profitability / cost-and-margin analysis driven entirely off posted invoices and standard cost, which maps most precisely to 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.x perform planning/management accounting and cost analysis); the module's surface lives under the Accounting Reporting menu and is gated to account.group_account_user, reinforcing the finance-analysis reading. 2.0 Develop and Manage Products/Services was considered because the manifest category is Sales/Sales and the subject is the product, but the module does not develop, price or manage products - it measures their financial margin - so 2.0 is at most secondary. The value driver is decision-support information, characteristic of support, not the throughput of a value chain.

standard_capabilities: per-product margin report built from posted customer invoices and vendor bills
configurable analysis window (from/to date) and invoice-state scope (paid / open+paid / draft+open+paid)
realised KPIs (turnover, total cost, total margin, margin rate) and expected KPIs (catalog sale, normal cost, expected margin, expected rate)
sales gap and purchase gap (expected vs realised) per product
multi-currency normalisation to company currency; multi-company scoping
list view with column sums + progressbar margin rates, KPI form page, and total_margin graph
typical_fits: quick product profitability review off the accounting ledger without a dedicated BI tool
spotting products where realised margin diverges from catalog/standard-cost expectation
period-over-period margin checks by changing the wizard date range
accounting/controlling users analysing margin alongside the Accounting Reporting menu
common_gaps: margin is invoice-based only: unbilled sale orders / POS / stock-valuation moves are not included (no link to sale.order, purchase.order or stock valuation)
expected margin uses current standard_price/list_price, not the price at invoice date (no historical cost layering)
no landed costs, discounts-at-line beyond price_subtotal, or analytic-account dimension in the aggregation
fields are non-stored, so grouping/pivoting beyond the provided list-sum/graph requires the Python read-group shim and cannot be used in arbitrary BI pivots
single hard-coded company-currency conversion; no cross-company consolidated view
drive_hints: odoo shell: w = env['product.margin'].create({'invoice_state':'open_paid'}); w.action_open_window()['context']  # see injected date_from/date_to/invoice_state

odoo shell: p = env['product.product'].browse(<id>).with_context(date_from='2024-01-01', date_to='2024-12-31', invoice_state='open_paid'); (p.turnover, p.total_cost, p.total_margin, p.total_margin_rate, p.expected_margin)
odoo shell: env['product.product'].with_context(date_from='2024-01-01', date_to='2024-12-31')._read_group([], [], ['turnover:sum','total_margin:sum'])  # exercises the non-stored-field group-sum shim
UI: Accounting > Reporting menu (account.account_reports_management_menu) > Product Margins…

open_questions: Exact semantics of res.currency._select_companies_rates() (the MATERIALIZED currency_rate CTE) and how it picks the rate row per invoice_date/company - defined in account/base, not here.
Whether downstream/enterprise modules add stock-valuation or sale/purchase-order based margin that this invoice-only report deliberately omits.
Behaviour of the margin fields when a product spans companies with different standard_price, given the single force_company scoping.
